title: Xanthe and the Cover
premise: Xanthe Reyes, a disgraced intelligence analyst scraping by in Lisbon, receives calls on a burner phone that no carrier can trace — from Felix Villalobos, a fixer she once loved, who died eight months ago in a car crash. Felix, alive and buried under a new identity, is working a deniable job for an embassy that exists on no map: a plot to stage an 'accidental' gas explosion that will kill a whistleblower and ignite a war pretext. As Xanthe follows the phone's breadcrumbs through forged documents, dead couriers, and a handler known only as the Cartographer, she realizes the attack is scheduled for the anniversary gala where she herself is bait — her presence lends the tragedy its 'random' victims. In the climax, Xanthe chooses truth over loyalty, exposing the operation at the cost of Felix's freedom, and the two walk away with nothing but each other and the untraceable phone still ringing.
about_author: Edmund Delacroix is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade inside the gray zones where deniability is policy. He writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Azores and has never confirmed which embassy he served.

chapters.title: The Phone That Rings Itself
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Broke and blacklisted in Lisbon, Xanthe finds a burner phone in her dead mother's storage unit. It rings: Felix Villalobos's voice — a man whose funeral she attended. He says only 'the Cartographer lied' before the line dies. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by impossible hope.

chapters.title: Eight Months Underground
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, flashback-threaded. Alive under a new name, Felix works deniable jobs for the Meridian Office, an embassy on no map. He planted the phone for Xanthe weeks ago, a failsafe he swore never to trigger. Now he has. Emotional beat: guilt — he used her once, and he's about to do it again.

chapters.title: The Cartographer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following Felix's cryptic directions to a shipping archive, she finds manifests for industrial gas routed to a building owned by a shell company — and a photograph of herself, circled in red, dated for the upcoming anniversary gala. Emotional beat: from skeptic to hunted in one afternoon.

chapters.title: Cases No One Wants Attributed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. His handler, the Cartographer, briefs the 'accident': a gas leak at the gala will kill whistleblower Ana Sotelo and a dozen bystanders. Felix realizes Xanthe's name is on the casualty list — her death gives the tragedy credibility. Emotional beat: cold professional detachment cracking into panic.

chapters.title: Two Dead Couriers
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A courier who agreed to testify turns up drowned; his contact is found in a burned car. Xanthe realizes the operation cleans up ahead of schedule and she's next. She calls the burner; Felix answers, and for the first time in eight months they speak plainly. Emotional beat: terror braided with old intimacy.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Xanthe infiltrates the gala's organizing committee using her analyst credentials; Felix maneuvers to swap the gas canisters for dummies. Both discover the Cartographer anticipated them — the security plan already names 'Reyes, X.' Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing you were inside the plan all along.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Buys
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Cartographer offers Felix everything: his old name, his old life, Xanthe's removal from the list — if he delivers Ana Sotelo personally. Felix, who built his career on loyalty to the Office, sees the offer for what it is: the price of becoming the Cartographer. Emotional beat: temptation and self-loathing.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes of Deniability
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Gala night. Xanthe gets Ana Sotelo out through the kitchen as Felix cuts the gas feed — but the Cartographer triggers a manual failsafe, and the building's alarms begin their countdown. Emotional beat: adrenaline, and the clarity that comes when every option is bad.

chapters.title: The Explosion That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, climax. Felix vents the gas into the river at the cost of exposing himself on camera; Xanthe livestreams the Cartographer's orders from a stolen radio. The 'accident' becomes evidence. The Cartographer is arrested by the very government that disavowed him. Emotional beat: triumph with a body count of consequences.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, weeks later. Felix testifies under immunity, loses everything but his name, and the Meridian Office quietly dissolves into paperwork. On a ferry out of Lisbon, the burner rings one last time — a wrong number, or an offer. They let it ring. Emotional beat: peace chosen over purpose, together.
